title: What if you swam in a pool of olive oil?
caption:
You'd sink in a pool of olive oil. 🫒🏊

Olive oil (about 0.91 g/cm³) is lighter than your body, even with your lungs full of air (about 0.97–0.99 g/cm³).

So in oil a 70 kg adult would still weigh about 4–5 kg and keep sinking. In water, the same full breath keeps you afloat.

Olive oil is also over 80× more viscous than water, so every kick drags.

What still floats? Pure body fat (about 0.90 g/cm³ at body temperature), barely: a 1 m block of it rides about 11 mm above the surface.

Send this to the friend who pours olive oil on everything.

A new impossible experiment every day.

⚠️ Don't try this. Oil can't hold you up the way water does, and oil breathed into the lungs can cause serious lung damage (lipoid pneumonia).

Computed: 70 kg / 1.058 = 66.2 L of tissue; + 4.8–6.0 L of air with lungs full (TLC 6 L, depending on whether residual air is already in 1.058) → 71.0–72.2 L → 0.970–0.986 g/cm³
Computed: weight in olive oil = 70 − 0.911 × (71.0…72.2) = 4.3–5.3 kg; in fresh water (0.998) = −0.9…−2.1 kg (floats, ≈1–2 kg spare lift)
Computed: pure fat (0.9007) in oil (0.911) floats with 1 − 0.9007/0.911 = 1.13 % of its height above the surface → 11 mm for a 1 m block
